## Fundamentals

::: {.lcm-layout-balanced}
::: {.lcm-slot .lcm-slot-panel}
[PHYSICAL INPUTS]{.lc-eyebrow}

::: {.incremental}
- Construction: conductor, insulation, screens and sheath.
- Material properties and temperature.
- Installation geometry, soil properties and neighbouring circuits.
:::
:::
::: {.lcm-slot .lcm-slot-panel}
[MODELLING BOUNDARY]{.lc-eyebrow}

Skin effect and earth return make the electrical response frequency-dependent.
Field data, modelling assumptions and numerical approximations contribute
different kinds of uncertainty; they should not be conflated.

A parameter sweep is a sensitivity study, not automatically a probability model.
:::
:::

## Cable constants · electrical meaning

::: {.lcm-layout-full-canvas}
::: {.lcm-slot .lcm-slot-panel}
[FREQUENCY-DOMAIN QUANTITIES]{.lc-eyebrow}

For a chosen frequency, the conventional decomposition is

$$
R=\operatorname{Re}(Z),\qquad L=\frac{\operatorname{Im}(Z)}{\omega},\qquad
G=\operatorname{Re}(Y),\qquad C=\frac{\operatorname{Im}(Y)}{\omega},
\quad \omega=2\pi f.
$$

For distributed line quantities, $Z$ and $Y$ are per-unit-length matrices.
Self and mutual entries belong to the declared conductor/terminal arrangement;
their units and connections are part of the model, not plot decoration.

The live line view shows real and imaginary matrix entries directly in Ω/m or S/m.
:::
:::

## OHL / UGC application case

::: {.lcm-layout-full-canvas}
::: {.lcm-slot .lcm-slot-panel}
[FROM CABLE TO NETWORK]{.lc-eyebrow}

Use the existing mixed overhead-line / underground-cable reference case.
Power-flow preparation solves the reference operating point and linearizes its
active devices. The following evaluation changes passive corridor elements.

::: {.incremental}
- Vary the underground share of a fixed corridor.
- Compare nominal length with a declared ±length variation.
- Inspect driving-point impedance at B5 with c2 eliminated, as defined by the existing operation.
:::

The three curves are deterministic sensitivity cases, not confidence bounds or
a new hosting-capacity solver. Active-device setpoints and earth specification
remain fixed in this curated demonstration.
:::
:::

## Conclusions

::: {.lcm-layout-full-canvas}
::: {.lcm-slot .lcm-slot-panel}
[PLANNING IMPLICATIONS]{.lc-eyebrow}

::: {.incremental}
- Frequency-dependent models expose movement in harmonic impedance and resonance.
- Sensitivity identifies where better material, geometry and field data matter.
- Statistical uncertainty models are needed before turning variations into risk-aware planning margins.
- Carry assumptions, units and execution provenance from cable construction into the system study.
:::
